predecessors.note: The Burma dossier (Konbaung kingdom, 1820-1885) loses these lands to British Empire / British Raj counterparts; this colony takes them in three steps.

the Tenasserim (Taninthayi) coast south of the Salween, with Moulmein

correction.text: Arakan and the Tenasserim coast, ceded 24 February 1826

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Treaty of Yandabo, 24 February 1826: Burma had to 'cede to the British Assam, Manipur, Rakhine(Arakan), and Taninthayi(Tenasserim) coast south of the Salween River'. Assam and Manipur are named in the treaty but lie outside modern Burma; they are left out and the pages opened do not say how the British administered them. The British Rule page gives no area.

the Tenasserim (Taninthayi) coast south of the Salween, with Moulmein

correction.text: Arakan, Tenasserim and Lower Burma (Pegu province) after 20 January 1853

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The proclamation of annexation was issued on 20 January 1853'; 'British East India Company takes control of Lower Burma'. The page puts the new frontier 'farther north at Myede'; the gazetteer region Lower Burma (about 74,000 km2) stops near Prome, so the strip to Myede is not in it.

correction.text: the whole colony of Burma, Upper Burma annexed 1 January 1886, as a province of British India and from 1 April 1937 a separate Crown Colony

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Burma was annexed by the British on January 1, 1886, by the proclamation of the Viceroy and Governor-General of India'; separated from British India 1 April 1937 (British Rule page). Shape = the modern country; the Shan States, Kachin and Chin hills enter with the dates in the ledger and the page gives no area to compare.

union.text: Arakan (Rakhine), conquered in 1825 and ceded at Yandabo
the Tenasserim (Taninthayi) coast south of the Salween, with Moulmein

region.text: Arakan and the Tenasserim coast south of the Salween

ledger.note: 1826: the Treaty of Yandabo makes Arakan and Tenasserim British. 'The Treaty of Yandabo was signed by General Campbell from the British side' on '24 February 1826'; Burma to 'cede to the British Assam, Manipur, Rakhine(Arakan), and Taninthayi(Tenasserim) coast south of the Salween River'. The British Rule page gives 'Establishment as Burma Division: 24 February 1826' and Moulmein as capital 1826-1852. The British took Arakan in 1825 (Mrauk-U defeated 1 April 1825). Assam and Manipur, named in the same treaty, are outside modern Burma and are not drawn here.

region.text: Lower Burma: Rangoon, Bassein, Pegu and Prome, the lower Irrawaddy valley

ledger.note: 1852: the Second Anglo-Burmese War opens. 'The first substantial blow ... on 5 April 1852'; 'Rangoon was occupied on 12 April', Bassein 19 May, Pegu 3 June, Prome 9 October (the page gives day and month; the year is implied by the war's dates 5 April 1852 - 20 January 1853).
1853: Rangoon replaces Moulmein as capital. Infobox: 'Moulmein (1826-1852) Rangoon (1853-1942; 1945-1948)'.

region.text: Lower Burma: Rangoon, Bassein, Pegu and Prome, the lower Irrawaddy valley

ledger.note: 1853: fighting ends. The infobox gives the war as '5 April 1852 - 20 January 1853'; 'No treaty was ever signed.'

region.text: Lower Burma: Rangoon, Bassein, Pegu and Prome, the lower Irrawaddy valley

ledger.note: 1853: Lower Burma annexed. 'The proclamation of annexation was issued on 20 January 1853'; the British Rule page says 'Lower Burma was annexed in 1852 after the Second Anglo-Burmese War' (the two pages differ by a year; the proclamation date is taken). The annexation covered 'the lower portion of the Irrawaddy River Valley, including Prome'.

1862: Arakan, Tenasserim and Pegu are made one province. 'Establishment as Burma Province: 31 January 1862'; the territories were 'designated as a chief commissioner's province known as British Burma in 1862'. First governor Sir Arthur Purves Phayre (1862-1867).

region.text: the Burmese kingdom of Mindon and Thibaw, Mandalay and the upper Irrawaddy valley, annexed on 1 January 1886

ledger.note: 1885: the Third Anglo-Burmese War. Infobox '7-29 November 1885'; the British Rule page has British troops entering Mandalay on 28 November 1885.

region.text: the Burmese kingdom of Mindon and Thibaw, Mandalay and the upper Irrawaddy valley, annexed on 1 January 1886

ledger.note: 1885: Mandalay falls and King Thibaw is taken prisoner (28 November), 'though the king was dethroned and exiled with the royal family to India'. Sporadic resistance 'continuing into 1887'; another sentence says the resistance lasted until 1896.

region.text: the tribal areas of the Kachin Hills and Chin Hills

ledger.note: 1886: the hill tracts. 'The British also extended their control into the tribal areas of the Kachin Hills and Chin Hills.' The page is silent on the year: 1886 bridges the annexation and the later pages.

region.text: the Burmese kingdom of Mindon and Thibaw, Mandalay and the upper Irrawaddy valley, annexed on 1 January 1886

ledger.note: 1886: Upper Burma annexed. 'Burma was annexed by the British on January 1, 1886, by the proclamation of the Viceroy and Governor-General of India'; the territories 'have become part of Her Majesty's dominions'. The British Rule page adds that Burma became 'a province of British India on 1 January 1886'. The outline is Cliopatria's 1884 Burma shape, the researcher's reading of 'Burma'.

region.text: the Shan States under their sawbwas

ledger.note: 1888: the Shan princely states. The page says the Shan States were under British rule and refers to the princely states 'established in 1888'; it is silent on 1886-1887. They stay under their sawbwas.

1922: Karenni joins the Federated Shan States arrangement. 'On 10 October 1922 the administrations of the Karenni states and the Shan states were officially clustered together' under one British commissioner. The page does not say how the Karenni states stood before.

1937: Burma is separated from British India. 'The British separated Burma Province from British India on 1 April 1937'; the infobox calls it a Crown Colony of the United Kingdom from that date. The British Raj dossier draws Burma inside the Raj to 1946; the renderer should not draw it twice.

1942: Japan occupies Burma. 'The Empire of Japan invaded Burma in December 1941 and by the end of 1942 controlled much of the colony'; the capital leaves Rangoon in 1942. 'In 1943, the State of Burma was proclaimed in Rangoon', a puppet state under Ba Maw. The Federated Shan States page has Kengtung captured by the Japanese on 27 May 1942.

region.text: Kengtung and part of Mongpan state

ledger.note: 1943: Thailand annexes Kengtung. 'on 18 August 1943 the Japanese government agreed to the Thai annexation of Kengtung and part of Mongpan state' (the Thai Phayap Army had also occupied part of the Karenni states in December 1942).

region.text: Kengtung and part of Mongpan state

ledger.note: 1945: Kengtung back. The page is silent on the return; 1945 is the researcher's bridge to 1948, when the Federated Shan States 'became Shan State and Kayah State of the Union of Burma'.
1945: the British retake Rangoon. 'Rangoon was recaptured in May 1945' (the page gives the capital's return, 1945-1948, but not the end of the Japanese hold on the rest of Burma).

region.text: the Federated Shan States, which became Shan State

ledger.note: 1948: the Shan and Karenni states join the Union. 'When Burma gained independence in 1948, the Federated Shan States became' Shan State and Kayah State.

region.text: the Karenni states, which became Kayah State

ledger.note: 1948: the Karenni states join the Union as Kayah State.
1948: independence. 'Burma became an independent republic on 4 January 1948.'

wars.name: First Anglo-Burmese War

zones.text: Arakan (Rakhine), conquered in 1825 and ceded at Yandabo
the Tenasserim (Taninthayi) coast south of the Salween, with Moulmein

wars.outcome: British victory: Treaty of Yandabo, 24 February 1826; Burma cedes Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim and pays an indemnity of one million pounds.
wars.note: War broke out 5 March 1824; Rangoon entered 11 May 1824; Arakan invaded 1 February 1825, Mrauk-U defeated 1 April 1825. The infobox says Manipur gained independence, the treaty list says it was ceded: the page does not reconcile them.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Burmese War

zones.text: Lower Burma: Rangoon, Bassein, Pegu and Prome, the lower Irrawaddy valley

wars.outcome: British victory: Lower Burma annexed by proclamation of 20 January 1853; no treaty signed.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Burmese War

zones.text: the Burmese kingdom of Mindon and Thibaw, Mandalay and the upper Irrawaddy valley, annexed on 1 January 1886

wars.outcome: British victory: Mandalay fell on 28 November 1885, Thibaw was exiled and Upper Burma annexed on 1 January 1886; resistance continued into 1887 (or to 1896 by the page's other sentence).

wars.name: Japanese conquest of Burma

zones.text: Kengtung and part of Mongpan state

wars.outcome: Japan invaded in December 1941 and held much of Burma by the end of 1942; Thailand annexed Kengtung on 18 August 1943; Rangoon recaptured in May 1945.
wars.note: The page dates the invasion and the Rangoon recapture only; the campaign years between are not narrated.

certainty.note: The Salween and the Myede frontier are described, not surveyed; the 1853 annexation had no treaty ('No treaty was ever signed').
The Shan, Kachin, Chin and Karenni frontiers are tribal and undated on the pages; the frontier with Thailand is not on any page opened.

notes:
Written 2026-10-20 by the se-03-x additions batch. A colony Cliopatria lacks as a dated conquest (1826, 1853, 1886); the shapes of the Konbaung kingdom are in burma.json (se-01 part) and of the Raj in british-raj (sa-06), which draws Burma inside the Raj to 1946. Five pages opened, the budget for a state of this size.
Unsettled: (1) Pages differ on Lower Burma: 'annexed in 1852' (British Rule page) against the proclamation of 20 January 1853 (Second War page, taken). The Burma dossier has the loss in 1853/1 as well. (2) The British Rule page gives no area, no annexation date for Arakan and Tenasserim, and nothing on the Chin, Kachin or Shan incorporation; 1886 for the hill tracts is confidence 1. (3) The 1853 frontier 'farther north at Myede' lies north of the gazetteer's Lower Burma region (which ends near Prome); a gap-filler may widen the 1853 keyframe with the Thayetmyo strip (Magway). (4) The Upper Burma outline is Cliopatria's Burma 1884 shape (437,000 km2), which includes Shan and Kachin land the British entered later; the dossier tints the Shan states from 1888 by vassal events, the Kachin and Chin hills come as a gain at confidence 1. (5) The Thai occupation of part of Karenni (December 1942) is only in a note; Kengtung's return to Burma is not on the page (confidence 1, 1945). (6) The 1943 State of Burma (Ba Maw) needs a dossier; the British Burma dossier records only the Japanese occupation. (7) Rulers: the page lists monarchs and two governors only, so identity.rulers is omitted. (8) Gazetteer names needed: Kengtung (Kyaingtong) as a place, about 21.29N 99.60E; Mongpan.
The counterpart 'burma' in the gains is the Konbaung dossier; its own ledger names british-empire and british-raj as the takers, so the loss and gain match by land and year, not by string.
